matter.title: Helios Renewables Pvt. Ltd. v. Northgrid Power Ltd.

entries.text: **Article 113** of the Limitation Act, 1963 prescribes a **three-year** period for suits for which no other period is provided, from when the right to sue accrues. The plaint relies on this (**Plaint ¶15, p. 3**).
**Section 12A** requires pre-institution mediation for commercial disputes. The plaint references this (**Plaint ¶12, p. 3**).

**PPA** dated **14.08.2021** between Helios Renewables (Seller) and Northgrid Power (Buyer) for 12 MW solar plant at Bhadla, Rajasthan, for 25 years at fixed tariff of **Rs. 2.95 per kWh** (**Plaint ¶3, p. 1**; **PPA p. 1**).

**Clause 9.1:** monthly invoice on JMR signed by both parties. **Clause 9.2:** payment within **30 days** of receipt. **Clause 9.3:** if JMR not signed within 7 days, SLDC reading final. **Clause 9.4:** dispute must be notified in writing within **15 days**; undisputed amount paid; if not disputed within 15 days, invoice deemed accepted. **Clause 9.6:** late payment surcharge **1% per month** simple (**PPA pp. 1-2**).

**Clause 14.1:** Buyer to establish and maintain a revolving **Letter of Credit of Rs. 6,00,00,000** before COD. **Clause 14.2:** failure to renew within 7 days of written demand is a **Buyer Event of Default** (**PPA p. 2**).

**Clause 16.1:** Buyer Event of Default includes (a) failure to pay undisputed invoice within **60 days** of Due Date; (b) failure to maintain LC. **Clause 16.3:** cure period of **60 days** after default notice. **Clause 16.4:** termination does not affect accrued rights (**PPA p. 2**).

**Clause 17.1:** Change in Law defined. **Clause 17.2:** affected party must give notice within **30 days**; parties negotiate tariff adjustment; Change in Law alone does not permit termination (**PPA pp. 2-3**).

**Clause 18.1:** Force Majeure defined. **Clause 18.2:** notice within **7 days**. **Clause 18.3:** if FM continues >180 days, either party may terminate with **30 days** notice. **Clause 18.5:** FM does not excuse payment for energy already supplied (**PPA p. 3**).

**Clause 22.1:** parties attempt amicable resolution through senior officers within **30 days** of written notice. **Clause 22.2:** unresolved disputes referred to **arbitration** by sole arbitrator under Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, seat New Delhi. **Clause 22.3:** tariff disputes to appropriate Electricity Regulatory Commission. **Clause 22.4:** pending dispute, parties continue performance and Buyer pays undisputed amounts (**PPA pp. 3-4**).
**Clause 23.2:** subject to Clause 22, courts at **New Delhi** have exclusive jurisdiction (**PPA p. 4**).
The Plant achieved **Commercial Operation Date (COD)** on **06.12.2021** (**Plaint ¶4, p. 2**).
Northgrid paid **Rs. 36,80,000** against the February 2023 invoice on **28.03.2023** (**Plaint ¶5, p. 2**).
The invoice for **April 2023** (first of ten invoices from April 2023 to 09.01.2024) fell due on **05.05.2023** and was not paid (**Plaint ¶¶6-7, pp. 2-3**; cause of action ¶14, p. 3).
Helios sent the first of several email reminders to Northgrid between **16.05.2023** and **20.12.2023** (**Plaint ¶7, p. 2**; **Annexure P-4**).
In an email dated **14.07.2023**, Northgrid stated payments were 'kept under review' on account of grid curtailment, but did not dispute any invoice (**Plaint ¶7, p. 2**).
Northgrid claims the Plant suffered a major outage between **02.08.2023** and **19.08.2023**, and that Helios billed for energy not supplied during that period (**Reply to notice ¶3, p. 2**).
Northgrid allowed the **Letter of Credit** to lapse on **30.09.2023** and did not renew it despite Helios' request (**Plaint ¶9, p. 2**; **Legal notice ¶4, p. 1**).
Northgrid's officers informed Helios' site team on **08.11.2023** that the meter readings for October 2023 were not accepted (**Reply to notice ¶2, p. 2**).
Northgrid's officers again informed Helios' site team on **12.12.2023** that the readings for November 2023 were not accepted (**Reply to notice ¶2, p. 2**).

Northgrid issued a notice dated **09.01.2024** purporting to terminate the PPA on grounds of **Change in Law** and **Force Majeure**, citing increase in inter-state transmission charges notified in 2023 (**Plaint ¶10, p. 3**; **Annexure P-5**).

Helios, through counsel, issued a legal notice dated **02.02.2024** demanding payment of **Rs. 3,68,40,000** (principal) plus late payment surcharge at **1% per month** under Clause 9.6, within 15 days (**Legal notice pp. 1-2**; **Plaint ¶11, p. 3**).

Northgrid replied on **21.02.2024** denying liability: disputed invoices for Oct-Dec 2023 (JMR not signed), claimed outage, said LC lapse due to Change in Law/FM, and invoked **Clause 22** for arbitration (**Reply to notice pp. 2-3**; **Plaint ¶11, p. 3**).

Helios initiated pre-institution mediation under **Section 12A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015** before the Delhi High Court Mediation and Conciliation Centre on **14.10.2024** (**Plaint ¶12, p. 3**).
Northgrid did not appear despite notice; a **non-starter report** was issued on **18.12.2024** (**Plaint ¶12, p. 3**; **Annexure P-8**).
Helios' Board of Directors passed a resolution on **24.02.2025** authorising Mr. Arvind Mehra to sign, verify and institute the suit (**Plaint ¶1, p. 1**).

Helios filed **CS(COMM) 412 of 2025** in the High Court of Delhi seeking recovery of **Rs. 4,82,00,000** (principal **Rs. 3,74,00,000** plus interest **Rs. 1,08,00,000** at 18% p.a.), and a declaration that the termination notice is illegal (**Plaint pp. 1-4**).

1963: Article 113 of the Limitation Act, 1963 prescribes a three-year period for suits for which no other period is provided, from when the right to sue accrues. The plaint relies on this (Plaint ¶15, p. 3).

1963

2015: Section 12A requires pre-institution mediation for commercial disputes. The plaint references this (Plaint ¶12, p. 3).

2015

14.08.2021: PPA dated 14.08.2021 between Helios Renewables (Seller) and Northgrid Power (Buyer) for 12 MW solar plant at Bhadla, Rajasthan, for 25 years at fixed tariff of Rs. 2.95 per kWh (Plaint ¶3, p. 1; PPA p. 1).

14.08.2021: Clause 9.1: monthly invoice on JMR signed by both parties. Clause 9.2: payment within 30 days of receipt. Clause 9.3: if JMR not signed within 7 days, SLDC reading final. Clause 9.4: dispute must be notified in writing within 15 days; undisputed amount paid; if not disputed within 15 days, invoice deemed accepted. Clause 9.6: late payment surcharge 1% per month simple (PPA pp. 1-2).

14.08.2021: Clause 14.1: Buyer to establish and maintain a revolving Letter of Credit of Rs. 6,00,00,000 before COD. Clause 14.2: failure to renew within 7 days of written demand is a Buyer Event of Default (PPA p. 2).

14.08.2021: Clause 16.1: Buyer Event of Default includes (a) failure to pay undisputed invoice within 60 days of Due Date; (b) failure to maintain LC. Clause 16.3: cure period of 60 days after default notice. Clause 16.4: termination does not affect accrued rights (PPA p. 2).

14.08.2021: Clause 17.1: Change in Law defined. Clause 17.2: affected party must give notice within 30 days; parties negotiate tariff adjustment; Change in Law alone does not permit termination (PPA pp. 2-3).

14.08.2021: Clause 18.1: Force Majeure defined. Clause 18.2: notice within 7 days. Clause 18.3: if FM continues >180 days, either party may terminate with 30 days notice. Clause 18.5: FM does not excuse payment for energy already supplied (PPA p. 3).

14.08.2021: Clause 22.1: parties attempt amicable resolution through senior officers within 30 days of written notice. Clause 22.2: unresolved disputes referred to arbitration by sole arbitrator under Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, seat New Delhi. Clause 22.3: tariff disputes to appropriate Electricity Regulatory Commission. Clause 22.4: pending dispute, parties continue performance and Buyer pays undisputed amounts (PPA pp. 3-4).

14.08.2021: Clause 23.2: subject to Clause 22, courts at New Delhi have exclusive jurisdiction (PPA p. 4).

2021

06.12.2021: The Plant achieved Commercial Operation Date (COD) on 06.12.2021 (Plaint ¶4, p. 2).

2023

28.03.2023: Northgrid paid Rs. 36,80,000 against the February 2023 invoice on 28.03.2023 (Plaint ¶5, p. 2).

05.05.2023: The invoice for April 2023 (first of ten invoices from April 2023 to 09.01.2024) fell due on 05.05.2023 and was not paid (Plaint ¶¶6-7, pp. 2-3; cause of action ¶14, p. 3).

16.05.2023: Helios sent the first of several email reminders to Northgrid between 16.05.2023 and 20.12.2023 (Plaint ¶7, p. 2; Annexure P-4).

14.07.2023: In an email dated 14.07.2023, Northgrid stated payments were 'kept under review' on account of grid curtailment, but did not dispute any invoice (Plaint ¶7, p. 2).

08.11.2023: Northgrid's officers informed Helios' site team on 08.11.2023 that the meter readings for October 2023 were not accepted (Reply to notice ¶2, p. 2).

entries.text: **Limitation Act, 1963:** a suit for money due has **3 years** (**Art. 113** and the residuary rules); a written acknowledgment or part-payment restarts the period (**ss. 18-19**). Time spent bona fide in a wrong forum is excluded (**s. 14**).

**Electricity Act, 2003:** tariff set or adopted under **ss. 62-63**; the State Commission regulates PPAs (**s. 86(1)(b)**) and refers disputes to arbitration (**s. 86(1)(f)**). Distribution licensees must keep payment security.

**Commercial Courts Act, 2015, s. 12A** (inserted 2018): a commercial suit with no urgent relief needs **pre-institution mediation** first; the Supreme Court has since treated this as mandatory. A **non-starter report** lets the plaintiff sue.
**PPA cl. 2 and 4:** Helios sells all output of its **12 MW** plant to Northgrid for **25 years** at a fixed tariff, with a **2% yearly escalation** (**cl. 11.3**).
**PPA cl. 9:** invoice monthly; pay within **30 days** (**5-day grace**, **cl. 9.4**); late payment carries **1.5% a month** interest (**cl. 9.6**). No right to withhold or set off is given.
**PPA cl. 14:** Northgrid keeps a **₹12 crore revolving letter of credit** for the whole term; failure to renew is an **event of default** (**cl. 14.2**) and Helios may draw on it.

entries.short: PPA cl. 17-18: change in law, force majeure
entries.text: **PPA cl. 17 (Change in Law)** and **cl. 18 (Force Majeure):** relief only for a notified change that hits the project, on prompt notice. Payment obligations are **not** excused by force majeure (**cl. 18.5**).
**PPA cl. 22:** technical and tariff disputes go to the State Commission or to arbitration. Helios reads it as not covering plain **non-payment of invoices**.

entries.label: Jun 2022
entries.text: **Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge) Rules, 2022:** a general framework for dues owed by distribution licensees to generators; the PPA rate of **1.5% a month** is claimed under the contract itself.

**Grid Code and CERC practice (general):** solar has **must-run** status; curtailment other than for grid security is generally compensated as **deemed generation**. A grid curtailment is no ground to stop paying for power already delivered.

**Order VIII r. 1 CPC (commercial suits):** written statement due in **30 days** of service, extendable to at most **120 days**; after that the right to file is lost. The Court’s summons order repeats this.
Helios and Northgrid sign the **Power Purchase Agreement** (**Annexure P-1**). Helios will sell all power from its 12 MW solar plant in Rajasthan for 25 years at a fixed tariff.
Northgrid’s bank issues the **₹12 crore letter of credit**, valid to 30.09.2023 and renewable (**Annexure P-3**), backing the monthly payments.
Joint certificate with the **state load dispatch centre**: the plant is running commercially (**COD**). Billing starts from here (**Annexure P-2**).
Helios raises **Invoice HR/22/001**, ₹38.6 lakh, for power supplied in December 2021 (**Plaint ¶6**; **Annexure P-5**).
Bank statement shows Northgrid paying the first invoice in full inside the 30-day window. It keeps paying on time for the next **13 months** (**Plaint ¶7**).
Helios notifies the agreed **2% escalation** (**cl. 11.3**). Northgrid does not object and pays the higher rate (**Annexure P-6**).
Helios raises **Invoice HR/23/014**, ₹41.2 lakh. This is the last invoice Northgrid pays (**Plaint ¶8**; **Annexure P-7**).
**Last payment:** the bank statement shows ₹41.2 lakh received. Nothing is paid after this date, and **limitation is counted from around here** (**Plaint ¶9**; **Annexure P-8**).
The **April 2023 invoice** (₹41.6 lakh) is not paid within the 5-day grace period, and no reason is given (**cl. 9.4**; **Plaint ¶10**).
Helios emails the **first reminder**, asks for the overdue amount and says **1.5% a month** will be charged (**cl. 9.6**; **Annexure P-9**).
Helios sends a **second reminder**, asks for a meeting and warns it may draw on the letter of credit (**Plaint ¶12**; **Annexure P-10**).
Northgrid says payments are **“kept under review”** because of grid curtailment. The agreement gives no right to hold payments (**Plaint ¶13**; **Annexure P-11**).
Helios sends a **statement of account**: five unpaid invoices of ₹41.6 lakh each, **₹2.08 crore** in all, payable in 15 days (**Plaint ¶14**; **Annexure P-12**).
Northgrid does **not renew the letter of credit**, which lapses. A separate breach of **cl. 14.2** (**Plaint ¶15**).

entries.short: Helios tries to encash the letter
entries.text: Helios asks the bank to pay under the letter of credit. The **bank refuses** as it has lapsed; Helios records this as loss of security (**Plaint ¶16**; **Annexure P-13**).
**Termination notice:** Northgrid claims **“change in law”** and **“deemed force majeure”** and says it may end the PPA. Helios denies both grounds (**Annexure P-14**; **cl. 17, 18**).
**Legal notice:** demands **₹3.74 crore** with interest in 15 days and rejects the termination as invalid (**Annexure P-15**; **Plaint ¶18**).
Northgrid’s **reply** disputes the invoices and says every dispute must go to **arbitration under cl. 22** (**Annexure P-16**).
**Rejoinder:** cl. 22 covers technical disputes only, not plain non-payment of invoices (**Annexure P-17**; **Plaint ¶20**).
Helios files its **s. 12A mediation application** before the Delhi High Court Mediation Centre (**Plaint ¶22**; **Annexure P-18**).
Northgrid **does not attend** either mediation sitting, despite notice of both dates (**Annexure P-19**).
The **mediation centre** issues a **non-starter report**, so the suit can now be filed (**Annexure P-19**).

entries.short: Suit filed in Delhi High Court
entries.text: **Suit filed:** CS(COMM) 412/2025 claims **₹4.82 crore**, being ₹3.74 crore of unpaid invoices plus interest and damages (**Plaint ¶1-4, 38**). Well within 3 years of the last payment.
The **registry** clears the plaint and gives it its case number.
**Summons issued** to Northgrid; written statement due within 30 days of receipt (**Order of 19.03.2025**).
**Next hearing:** listed before the **Joint Registrar** for admission and denial of documents (**Order of 19.03.2025**).

input.inSum: Helios supplied power and billed on time under a 25-year PPA from 2021, and Northgrid paid until 28.03.2023. Pre-suit mediation failed because Northgrid stayed away. The ₹4.82 crore suit was filed on 06.03.2025, inside the 3-year period, and the next date is 07.05.2025.

2018: Commercial Courts Act, 2015, s. 12A (inserted 2018): a commercial suit with no urgent relief needs pre-institution mediation first; the Supreme Court has since treated this as mandatory. A non-starter report lets the plaintiff sue.

2018

14.08.2021: PPA cl. 2 and 4: Helios sells all output of its 12 MW plant to Northgrid for 25 years at a fixed tariff, with a 2% yearly escalation (cl. 11.3).

14.08.2021: PPA cl. 9: invoice monthly; pay within 30 days (5-day grace, cl. 9.4); late payment carries 1.5% a month interest (cl. 9.6). No right to withhold or set off is given.

14.08.2021: PPA cl. 14: Northgrid keeps a ₹12 crore revolving letter of credit for the whole term; failure to renew is an event of default (cl. 14.2) and Helios may draw on it.

14.08.2021: PPA cl. 17 (Change in Law) and cl. 18 (Force Majeure): relief only for a notified change that hits the project, on prompt notice. Payment obligations are not excused by force majeure (cl. 18.5).

14.08.2021: PPA cl. 22: technical and tariff disputes go to the State Commission or to arbitration. Helios reads it as not covering plain non-payment of invoices.

2021

14.08.2021: Helios and Northgrid sign the Power Purchase Agreement (Annexure P-1). Helios will sell all power from its 12 MW solar plant in Rajasthan for 25 years at a fixed tariff.

05.10.2021: Northgrid’s bank issues the ₹12 crore letter of credit, valid to 30.09.2023 and renewable (Annexure P-3), backing the monthly payments.

06.12.2021: Joint certificate with the state load dispatch centre: the plant is running commercially (COD). Billing starts from here (Annexure P-2).

Jun 2022: Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge) Rules, 2022: a general framework for dues owed by distribution licensees to generators; the PPA rate of 1.5% a month is claimed under the contract itself.

2022

05.01.2022: Helios raises Invoice HR/22/001, ₹38.6 lakh, for power supplied in December 2021 (Plaint ¶6; Annexure P-5).

02.02.2022: Bank statement shows Northgrid paying the first invoice in full inside the 30-day window. It keeps paying on time for the next 13 months (Plaint ¶7).

18.07.2022: Helios notifies the agreed 2% escalation (cl. 11.3). Northgrid does not object and pays the higher rate (Annexure P-6).

2023: Grid Code and CERC practice (general): solar has must-run status; curtailment other than for grid security is generally compensated as deemed generation. A grid curtailment is no ground to stop paying for power already delivered.

2023

06.02.2023: Helios raises Invoice HR/23/014, ₹41.2 lakh. This is the last invoice Northgrid pays (Plaint ¶8; Annexure P-7).

05.05.2023: The April 2023 invoice (₹41.6 lakh) is not paid within the 5-day grace period, and no reason is given (cl. 9.4; Plaint ¶10).

16.05.2023: Helios emails the first reminder, asks for the overdue amount and says 1.5% a month will be charged (cl. 9.6; Annexure P-9).

20.06.2023: Helios sends a second reminder, asks for a meeting and warns it may draw on the letter of credit (Plaint ¶12; Annexure P-10).

14.07.2023: Northgrid says payments are “kept under review” because of grid curtailment. The agreement gives no right to hold payments (Plaint ¶13; Annexure P-11).

04.09.2023: Helios sends a statement of account: five unpaid invoices of ₹41.6 lakh each, ₹2.08 crore in all, payable in 15 days (Plaint ¶14; Annexure P-12).

30.09.2023: Northgrid does not renew the letter of credit, which lapses. A separate breach of cl. 14.2 (Plaint ¶15).

20.11.2023: Helios asks the bank to pay under the letter of credit. The bank refuses as it has lapsed; Helios records this as loss of security (Plaint ¶16; Annexure P-13).

2024

09.01.2024: Termination notice: Northgrid claims “change in law” and “deemed force majeure” and says it may end the PPA. Helios denies both grounds (Annexure P-14; cl. 17, 18).

02.02.2024: Legal notice: demands ₹3.74 crore with interest in 15 days and rejects the termination as invalid (Annexure P-15; Plaint ¶18).

03.12.2024: Northgrid does not attend either mediation sitting, despite notice of both dates (Annexure P-19).

18.12.2024: The mediation centre issues a non-starter report, so the suit can now be filed (Annexure P-19).

19.03.2025: Order VIII r. 1 CPC (commercial suits): written statement due in 30 days of service, extendable to at most 120 days; after that the right to file is lost. The Court’s summons order repeats this.

06.03.2025: Suit filed: CS(COMM) 412/2025 claims ₹4.82 crore, being ₹3.74 crore of unpaid invoices plus interest and damages (Plaint ¶1-4, 38). Well within 3 years of the last payment.

12.03.2025: The registry clears the plaint and gives it its case number.

19.03.2025: Summons issued to Northgrid; written statement due within 30 days of receipt (Order of 19.03.2025).

07.05.2025: Next hearing: listed before the Joint Registrar for admission and denial of documents (Order of 19.03.2025).

Key:  Rules / orders   |   Helios’s own acts   |   Third parties   |   Adverse action

It then stopped paying, let the letter of credit lapse and, in January 2024, tried to end the PPA on “change in law” and force majeure grounds that the PPA does not support for payment dues.
